summary: Advance research to inspect specific benchmark papers for descriptive evidence, as the strict empirical comparison hypothesis is unfeasible.
objective: Execute a bounded research task: Identify and inspect 4 sources (papers or repos) that provide empirical data comparing dynamic memory consolidation policies against a defined static baseline (e.g., append-only) under comparable token budgets. Measure task success and hallucination rates. Limit to 4 sources; do not implement code.
content: The previous bounded task failed to find 4 sources comparing dynamic vs. static memory under fixed token budgets. Literature lacks controlled experiments matching resource constraints. Per protocol, we must now inspect sources describing agent memory approaches (dynamic vs. static) on general benchmarks, explicitly noting missing controls. We will search for papers reporting task success/hallucination rates on standard agent benchmarks (e.g., BigBench, GSM8K) to gather descriptive performance data without inferring superiority without direct baseline comparison.
nextTask: Execute a bounded research task: Identify and inspect 4 sources (papers or repos) that describe agent memory management approaches (dynamic vs. static) and document their reported performance on general benchmarks, explicitly noting where direct baseline comparisons or token-budget controls are missing. Limit to 4 sources; do not implement code.
searchQueries: agent memory management benchmarks task success hallucination rates
dynamic vs static agent memory performance comparison
episodic memory retrieval benchmarks agent systems
context window management agent evaluation benchmarks

wiki.lesson: If a hypothesis requires an experimental condition (e.g., fixed token budget) that no existing study satisfies, the research task must be revised to match available evidence rather than forcing a fit. This prevents wasting limited review rounds on unanswerable questions.
